title: HUNTER: Did apartment conditions trigger Stoney Creek bloodbath?
article: This is how someone can die.
A young couple - a 27-year-old woman and a 28-year-old man - were not happy with the conditions in their basement apartment at 322 Jones Rd. in Stoney Creek.
She was an educational assistant with a Brant County school board and he was an electrician in Hamilton. They were engaged to be married, but it would be a festive date the pair would never make.
Late on a sunny Saturday afternoon, according to cops, tensions with landlord Terry Brekka boiled over and ended in tragedy.

Brekka, who lived in the largely industrial area for about 20 years, owned a number of registered handguns and long guns. Neither Brekka nor the thus far unnamed couple had any interaction with the cops.
Shortly after 10 p.m., the couple and Brekka were all dead.
"It's a rough one," Hamilton Police homicide Det.-Sgt. Steve Bereziuk told the Toronto Sun .
When officers arrived, they found the man and woman shot to death on the front lawn.
"Both were deceased at the scene without vital signs," Bereziuk said.
The emergency response unit was called in "to contain the home." Barricaded inside was the 57-year-old Brekka, who appalled neighbours called "quiet."
Bereziuk said cops talked to the shooter several times over several hours in an attempt to "end the standoff peacefully."
"He then began shooting at police and that led to the interaction," the veteran detective said. "And the SIU (Special Investigations Unit) invoked its mandate."
While Bereziuk was restricted by the SIU mandate in offering details about the triggerman, he offered an explanation about what may have sparked the bloodshed.
"They had complained about (what the couple believed) were unhealthy conditions in the apartment," he said. "None of these people had ever had contact with the police."
Now the families of the dead and the killer are struggling to come to terms with what appears to be a horrifying moment of madness.

"For the families, it's a very difficult situation; they are completely broken-hearted and grief-stricken," Bereziuk said, adding that the community is "also shocked and upset by this ... this is something that doesn't happen here. It's a very, very unfortunate tragedy."
On Monday, the area around Jones Rd. was filled with the hum of business. Cops were still on the scene, so was the media and so were gawkers.

The area isn't a neighbourhood in the way one normally thinks of a neighbourhood. It's a mix of some nice homes, some run-down ones and a lot of businesses, such as a LaForge cement plant, storage units, trucking yards and light manufacturing.
Transports roll through around the clock.
At the neat two-storey home, the front grass where the young couple perished as they ran for their lives remains uncut. A smashed-in garage door and a broken front door littered the lawn.

The scene of the double murder is less than 2 km from the scene of the murder of B.C. man Tyler Pratt, 39, and the attempted murder of his fiancee on Feb. 28, 2021. Pratt's pregnant fiancee survived, but lost her baby.
Oliver Karafa and Yun "Lucy" Lu Li are charged with first-degree murder.
Back on Jones Rd., there is the hubbub, but hiding in the shadows is the inexplicable deaths of three people.
